logic.note: Runs the real compiled firmware in Renode (an open-source emulator, MIT) in a local Docker container, in lockstep with Jumper's clock. GPIO (with pin interrupts), Serial, Wire and SPI reach Jumper's parts through Jumper's bridge (every signal time-stamped to the instruction).

timing.note: Virtual time counts one instruction per core clock cycle at the board's clock (no pipeline, wait-state or cache timing), so delay(), millis() and timers are exact in virtual time and busy loops are close. A part's reaction to a pin edge lands at the next simulation step (1 ms by default), not mid-step. Measured on an M4 Max: about 0.5 to 1x real time with 1 ms steps (busy-wait delay() runs every instruction).

analog.note: Pins are ideal sources with about 50 Ω output resistance and 40 kΩ pull-ups; inputs switch at 0.3 / 0.7 x 3.3 V. analogRead on ADC1's pins converts the solved net voltage to 12 bits against an ideal 3.3 V reference at once (no sampling time, noise or non-linearity).

power.note: USB (power.usb) puts 5 V on the 5V pin; the on-board LDO makes 3V3 from it (dropout typical). The board draws its typical current; per-pin current above the limit is flagged. Brownout and sleep currents are not simulated.

emulates: STM32F103C8 Cortex-M core and the peripherals Arduino sketches use, in Renode 1.17 (jumper/renode image)
Digital I/O with pull-ups and pin interrupts (attachInterrupt)
Serial (the board's console UART) with per-byte virtual time
Wire (I2C master) to the I2C parts on the board's default pins
SPI (master) to the SPI parts on the board's default pins
analogRead on ADC1 channels (Jumper's ADC model / Renode's STM32 ADC fed by Jumper)
analogWrite / Servo / tone through the timers' PWM outputs where Renode routes them to the pin
ADC1 through Jumper's STM32F1 ADC model (Renode has none for the F1)
Clock setup through Jumper's minimal RCC / FLASH models (Renode has no F1 RCC)
doesNotEmulate: Other UARTs than the console (Serial2, Serial3) reaching parts
Wire / SPI on other than the default pins (Wire.setSDA, SPI.setMOSI)
USB (the board's USB device: USB CDC Serial, HID)
Flash / EEPROM emulation persisting across a reset
The reset button and the NRST pin
The RTC on its 32.768 kHz crystal and VBAT
Bus electrical detail (clock stretching, rise times)
The 64 / 128 KB flash difference of real C8 chips (often 128 KB)
testOnRealDevice: Upload: DFU / ST-LINK / serial bootloader on your computer
Analog readings: the real ADC has offset, noise and sampling-time effects
Timing-critical code: the emulator counts one cycle per instruction
5 V parts: only the FT pins tolerate 5 V as inputs; outputs are 3.3 V

I2C scanners: on these boards each absent address costs about 130 ms of virtual time in the emulator (Renode's STM32 I2C model plus STM32duino's timeout), so a full scan is slow; addressed devices answer at full speed
